claim: The deterministic preparation transaction emits and consumes the canonical 100-byte Schnorr ALL|FORKID P2PKH authorization for deposit, transfer, and withdrawal. Its vout-0 binding and vout-1 fee siblings share the wire-order double-SHA256 parent, and its fee/change accounting is exact at the requested feerate.

tests.name: BCH-2026 standard VM accepts each real locally signed preparation
wire/display outpoint boundary
tests.expected: one reversal at libauth object boundary; child siblings use raw double-SHA256 wire order

tests.name: P2PKH authorization mutations
tests.expected: wrong parent, vout, alternate sighash, mismatched key, diverted change, and signature mutation reject

tests.name: canonical dust/change accounting
tests.expected: 546-satoshi change accepted; 545-satoshi change rejected; fee equals bytes times feerate

tests.name: settlement preparation-pair structural checks
tests.expected: same parent, vout 0 binding, vout 1 fee, canonical source lock/unlock, and exact change lock
tests.observed: existing settlement package test suite passed; wrong parent/vout, source/key mismatch, diverted change, and malformed unlock cases rejected

limitations: This is local Libauth BCH-2026 standard-VM evidence for the one-input preparation P2PKH transaction, not BCHN peer relay or Chipnet inclusion evidence.

The complete ten-input settlement transaction remains structurally checked only here; it cannot be claimed VM-valid until the real PF7 verifier and binding/state covenant inputs are present and executed together.
This observation neither establishes G2 nor changes its 59000-byte complete-settlement gate.
